metrics.definition: SUM(sale_price) over items whose status is not Cancelled or Returned. Shipped, Complete and Processing items count.
Items whose status is not Cancelled or Returned, and the orders that have at least one such item. Every metric below uses counted items unless it says otherwise.
Gross profit divided by revenue, as a percentage.
Revenue divided by the number of distinct counted orders.
Counted items divided by the number of distinct counted orders.
Returned items divided by items that were not Cancelled.
Cancelled items divided by all items.
Share of customers with a counted order in the period who have two or more distinct counted orders in that period.

A customer has churned when their last counted order is more than 90 days before the end of the period (today if the period runs to today). Churn rate is churned customers divided by customers with at least one counted order before the end of the period.

time_rules.definition: Every time-based metric uses the order date, order_created_at. Use DATE(order_created_at) for dates. Never use shipped, delivered or returned dates for periods.

time_rules.term: this month, this quarter, this year
time_rules.definition: From the first day of the current calendar month, quarter or year up to today.
1 January of the current year up to today.

time_rules.term: last month, last quarter, last year
time_rules.definition: The previous complete calendar month, quarter or year.

Calendar quarters: Q1 is January to March, Q2 April to June, Q3 July to September, Q4 October to December. With no year given, use the current year if the quarter has started, otherwise the previous year.
The same dates one year earlier, so a partial period is compared with the same partial period.

business_terms.definition: A segment, never a list of people: the top 10% of customers by revenue in the period. Describe it by size, share of revenue, age bands, gender and locations.
Customers with at least one counted order in the period.
Customers whose first counted order falls in the period.

scope_rules.definition: A brand manager's figures cover only their own brands. A total means the total for their brands, not the company.
An order can hold items from several brands. A brand manager sees only their own items in it, so order value, AOV and basket size are their brands' share of each order.
Company-wide figures are not available to brand managers. Don't compare their brands with the company total.
